title: Toggle Link Chain
ingredient: fresh yellow genda marigolds on a cotton thread, loose petals
rhyme: the chain is a garland you wear: marigold gold = 18k gold tone
notes: Clasp exact (spring-gate ring with gate and push-pin, pave bar threaded through), ring to link 1.4 (true 1.36). Loose petals read as smooth single petals rather than ruffled marigold florets in every attempt; 01b is the most natural. Calm plaster on the left for the feed line.

title: Baguette Tennis Necklace
ingredient: Agra petha: translucent sugar-crusted rectangles on an old brass plate
rhyme: icy clear crosswise baguettes = the translucent glint of petha blocks
notes: Construction exact at full size: crosswise baguettes in gold box settings with side windows and four claws, box clasp with tongue. Petha reads true (translucent, sugar crust). Calm plaster upper left.

title: Woven Gold Hoops
ingredient: three ripe golden wheat ears, loose grains and a bristle
rhyme: the braid of the hoops = the plaited chevron rows of a wheat ear, same warm gold
notes: Braid exact (interlaced polished strands), flat disc inside the top under the hinged latch; hoops a third of a wheat ear, true scale. Calm plaster left.

title: Verdant Eternity Band
ingredient: freshly shelled hara chana in an old brass katori, a papery pod
rhyme: oval emerald stones = plump green chickpeas, same fresh green and shape
notes: Ring exact: emerald ovals in 4 claws, the S-wave of pave weaving between them, open back with looped tips. Chickpeas about 8mm, true scale. Variant b drew the chickpeas olive-size.

title: Cushion Halo Ring
ingredient: kaju katli with silver varq, a stack on crinkled butter paper and one loose diamond, torn varq flakes
rhyme: silver varq = rhodium silver tone; the katli diamond = the cushion halo turned 45 degrees
notes: Halo exact in 06b: one row of small stones with bead claws round a 4-claw round centre, pave shoulders, plain polished shank, cool silver. 06a drew a denser double-looking halo. Ring about 1.2x against a standard katli, reads true. Feed crop starts higher (200px) so the katli stack is whole.

title: Baguette Tennis Bracelet
ingredient: a soft mound of raw long-grain basmati rice with a trail of single grains spilling into the bracelet
rhyme: slim translucent rice grains = slim icy crosswise baguettes, same size and shape
notes: Construction exact: emerald-cut baguettes crosswise in gold box settings with 4 claws, box clasp with fold-over safety. Grain to baguette width 0.6 (true 0.6), length 1.4 (true 1.15): honest scale. 07b calmer but the rice barely meets the bracelet.

title: Baguette Huggies
ingredient: a loose heap of pistachio pieces with rose-purple skins, a few loose slivers in front
rhyme: green pistachio = emerald baguettes; slim slivers = slim crosswise stones; pista is the garnish of every mithai
notes: Low 20-degree camera for variety. Construction exact: 7 crosswise emerald-cut baguettes with shared bar claws and bead tips on the lower front, hinge and snap bar visible, plain polished upper half. Pistachio reads real but pinker than the stones, so the colour rhyme is softer than the earlier plates. 08b turned the standing huggie edge-on into a column of stones.

title: Bold Nocturne Chain
ingredient: broken chunks of golden Kolhapuri jaggery (gur) with crumbs
rhyme: honey-gold gur = warm polished gold; chunky blocks = chunky links; gur, good
notes: Links exact: elongated rounded rectangles with flattened sides, each threaded through the next, one pave link the same size. Gur reads real (crystalline, sugary bloom), large but plausible at about 2.5 links. 09a wedged the chain end between the gur chunks. First cool ground of the set.

title: Bold Nocturne Bracelet
ingredient: a soft cone of haldi powder and two fresh turmeric roots, one snapped to its orange core
rhyme: haldi yellow = 18k gold tone; wedding season, the haldi ceremony
notes: 10a had the best layout but two four-point star glints on the pave link and frosted link interiors; 10b frosted too. Reshot with both faults named: 10c is clean, links polished inside and out, one pave link, lobster clasp and extender tag exact. Links match a turmeric finger in thickness.

title: Halo Curve Ring
ingredient: almonds, some with their brown skins and some soaked and peeled, one slipped skin; one brown and one peeled almond at the ring
rhyme: tiger eye = the striated brown almond skin; champagne crystal = the peeled almond; the Indian morning badam
notes: Ring exact: thin open bypass wire, banded tiger eye and faceted champagne crystal in unmatched slim bezels; each stone about half an almond, true scale. The brown almond lies under the tiger eye and the peeled one under the crystal, mirroring the pair. 11a crowded the top with the heap.

title: Kiss Knot Bangle
ingredient: three golden Diwali chakli flecked with sesame, one broken in half, crumbs
rhyme: the ribbed gold coil = the piped ridges of a golden chakli spiral; Diwali faral season
notes: Bangle exact: continuous finely ribbed tubogas coil bound by one polished X at the front. Chakli read real (rough fried ridges, black sesame). 12a equally true but the chakli crowd the top. First sage ground. Gold reads a touch rosy in the warm light.

title: Brushed Gold Huggies
ingredient: two rava laddoos, one topped with a cashew and one broken open, crumbs
rhyme: the pale satin-brushed gold = the pale matte gold of a ghee-roasted rava laddoo; Diwali
notes: 16a/16b drew the huggies 2.5 to 3 times too large against the cashew. Reshot with the earrings touching the laddoos at the same depth and a critical-scale block: 16c is about 1.3x true (huggie a third of a laddoo). Brushed satin finish and pale gold true; hinge side visible.

title: Rivière Eternal Bracelet
ingredient: an old steel katori of dry sabudana (sago), grains and sago dust spilled beside the bracelet
rhyme: round 3-4mm stones = round 3mm sago grains, one sparkling and one chalky white
notes: Round one drew drilled bead-like sago (reads as beads or pearls) and star glints. Round two in a steel katori read as food but the soaked clump looked like jelly. Round three, dry only: 17f reads as sago (irregular chalky grains, powder), grains the size of the stones, bracelet exact with box clasp and fold-over safety, no glints.

title: Molten Panel Bracelet
ingredient: a heap of golden chana dal (split Bengal gram), loose dal beside the bracelet
rhyme: each 6mm flat gold oval plate = one split chana dal, same size, shape and golden colour
notes: Bracelet exact: five staggered brick-set rows of flat oval plates, box clasp; plate about one dal, true scale. Line twists the Hindi idiom daal mein kuch kaala hai. 21a rendered a window frame in the background and laid the band open and straight.

title: Torsade Pearl Cuff
ingredient: a heap of makhana (puffed lotus seeds), one makhana beside each pearl
rhyme: the two round creamy white shell pearls = round creamy white makhana, the same size and white
notes: Cuff exact: solid twisted cable, two-row pave collars split by a gold rib, one shell pearl at each end facing across the opening. Makhana about 1.4x a pearl, real. 22a pushed the makhana tight against the ends. Makhana moved here from the baroque shell bracelet (31 now pairs with cowrie shells).

title: Bold Dome Huggies
ingredient: a small group of golden pani puri shells (golgappe), one cracked open, crisp crumbs
rhyme: the swelling polished gold domes = the puffed golden domes of the puris
notes: 26a/26b drew the huggies about 2x against the 4cm puri. Reshot touching the puri at the same depth with a critical-scale block: 26c about 1.4x true. Lying hoop shows the swelling dome and hinge; the standing one reads more even. 26d rendered a window in the background.

title: Torsade Huggies
ingredient: two crossed twisted khari puff-pastry straws, a broken piece, golden flakes
rhyme: the twisted gold rope ridges = the twist of golden khari pastry; khari is the chai-time biscuit
notes: Huggies exact: domed, twisted polished ridges all round, hinge visible. Listing size 20x18mm, so about 1.3x against a 2cm khari straw. 27a crowded three straws over the earrings.

title: Serpentine Whisper Chain
ingredient: coarse rock salt crystals (khada namak), a loose heap with two crystals beside the stone
rhyme: the clear cushion stone among clear salt crystals, so the eye has to look twice to find the jewel; the snake chain lies in its own serpentine S
notes: 30b: one cushion stone in four ball-tipped claws with the open basket gallery and a polished bail, true scaled snake chain at about a fifth of the stone width, chain enters from the right edge in one S. Stone about the size of the biggest crystals. 30a looped the chain twice down from the top edge across the calm top left. Feed crop lowered to 340 so the crystals at the stone keep a margin; the top of the heap bleeds off the edge.

title: Baroque Shell Bracelet
ingredient: seven cowrie shells thrown as in pachisi, backs and toothed mouths, one touching a pearl
ground: honey-cream lime plaster with a soft diagonal window shadow
rhyme: glossy cowrie beside lustrous white shell pearl, ivory and honey with the gold toggle; cowries were dice, small change and a token of luck
notes: 31a turned the strand into about 16 small ridged oval pearls with rondelles, dwarfed by the cowries. Reshot with EXACTLY NINE big flat baroque pearls the size of a cowrie (31c, 31d both faithful), but 31b from the first batch had already come back right: nine flat irregular pearls, one small gold bead between each, round toggle and T-bar, one larger drop on a ball-headed pin. 31d hangs the drop below the 4:5 window; 31c looks arranged rather than thrown.

title: Petite Square Huggies
ingredient: two cubes of soan papdi, one broken open, loose flaky threads, one flake touching a huggie
rhyme: the squared huggie = the square of a soan papdi cube, golden flake against polished gold; soan papdi is the Diwali box everybody passes on
notes: 32a: squared hoops with rounded corners in a smooth thick polished tube, hinge wire and seam as in the listing macro, four tiny pearls on the standing hoop (two each side). Huggie about 0.5 of a cube side against 0.42 true, the earrings sit nearer the lens. A pistachio fleck crept onto one cube in both frames. 32b drew one cube as dense fudge and the hoops about 1.4x. The cubes take the top left of the Feed, so the block sits bottom left under the standing hoop.

title: Rivière Hoops
ingredient: whole cashews (kaju), a loose scatter with one lying beside the flat hoop
rhyme: the open C of stones curves exactly like a cashew; kaju is always the first thing gone from a Diwali dry-fruit box
notes: Shot from the live listing refs (open hoop on a post, oval stones in milgrain cups); the Edition One riviere refs show an older hinged claw-set huggie. 33a: open C, one row of oval stones edge to edge in beaded cups, fine post; hoop about 1.25x a cashew against 1.2-1.4 true. Stones on the flat hoop read a little soft in the window light. 33b nested the pair and lost the top cashew to the crop.

title: Emerald Square Ear Cuff
ingredient: the corner of a square of fresh banana leaf with three beads of water
rhyme: one small square green stone beside one big square green leaf; meals are served on banana leaf
notes: Sold as one cuff (listing copy: one green square), so one cuff is shown though the listing hero has two. 34a/34b drew the cuff about 2x against a 6cm leaf. Reshot with a 10cm leaf bleeding off the frame and the water beads as referent. 34d keeps the listing proportions (stone about 0.37 of the C) and true size (beads about 4mm, stone about 5mm, C about 14mm); its gold measures hue 34 against 32-33 in the listing photos, so the rosy look is only the green around it. 34c stood the cuff up with a tight C that made the stone about 1.5x too big for its band.

title: Pear Point Open Cuff
ingredient: loose pink desi rose petals beaded with rose water, two drops on the plaster, one petal touching the cuff
rhyme: the two clear pear stones = two drops of gulab jal on rose petals
notes: 35a/35b set both pears with their tips facing each other across the gap; in the listing each point tucks into the V of the band end and the rounded ends face the gap (the brief had said pointing toward each other). Reshot with the orientation spelled out: 35c and 35d both right. 35c kept for the softer plaster and a real spectral caustic thrown by the right stone. Cuff about 6cm, pears about 8mm against petals of 2.5cm.

title: Bold Nocturne Drops
ingredient: til chikki, four sesame-and-jaggery pieces, loose seeds and a shard, one piece touching a pavé link
rhyme: the pavé link, tiny white stones packed in gold = sesame packed in golden jaggery
notes: The listing hero and macro show three parts per earring: a polished oval on the post, a smaller polished connector and the big pavé link (the brief wrongly said two links). 36a draws all three on both earrings with the posts; 36b drops the connector on one earring. Earring about 1.3-1.5x against a 35mm chikki piece, within what chikki sizes allow. The line avoids set-in-gold wording because the piece is gold tone.

title: Marquise Drop Choker
ingredient: a brass katori of chashni (sugar syrup) with one thread falling from a steel spoon
rhyme: the fine drop chain with its two pears = ek taar ki chashni, the one-thread test of Indian sweet-making; brass, syrup and gold in one warm key
notes: Collar is the ribbed round snake collar of the listing (the older lock said smooth). 37a: ribbed collar, marquise set sideways in claws, fine cable drop with a small pear halfway and one at the end, both pointing down; the collar circles the katori. One straight thread falls from the spoon, the one-thread test. 37b coils the syrup into a honey ribbon and crops the bowl. The spoon is held from out of frame.

title: Droplet Open Cuff
ingredient: gond (edible acacia gum), glassy tears and frosted crackled nuggets, one tear beside the cuff
rhyme: the cuff ends in a polished ball and a gold teardrop = the amber tears of gond, the gum of Indian winter laddoos
notes: 38a fused a gond tear onto the cuff in place of its gold teardrop. 38b was faithful but the teardrop was thin (0.57 of the ball against about 0.9 in the listing) and the gond looked like amber glass. Reshot asking for a full teardrop almost as wide as the ball, both ends solid metal, and natural gond with frosted crackled skins: 38c has the ball and a smooth swelling teardrop at about 0.65, natural gond, and an amber reflection in the gold. 38d pulled the gond into long glassy strings.

title: Petal Flower Studs
ingredient: whole cloves (laung), a loose heap with three lying apart, one head turned to the camera
rhyme: the four-petal stud = the four-pointed head of a clove; in Punjabi the laung nose stud is named after the clove
notes: 39a: three round stones and one pear in claws round a polished gold disc, butterfly backs, exactly as the listing macro. Stud about 0.9 of a clove in length against 0.8-0.95 true. Asked for clay plaster, came back warm cream, which keeps the cloves dark and the gold warm. 39b drew the studs smaller and softer with more spice dust.

title: Fine Tennis Bracelet
ingredient: yellow mustard seeds (peeli rai), a spill with a band of seeds following the bracelet
rhyme: one line of tiny round stones beside one line of tiny round mustard seeds; rai goes into every tadka, as the bracelet goes with every outfit
notes: 40b: one row of round stones in four-claw gold cups edge to edge, a real box clasp with tongue and latch, stones about 1.5 seeds wide (3mm against 2mm seeds); the seeds run as a band parallel to the bracelet. 40a scattered the seeds naturally but put a four-point star glint on one stone by the clasp.

title: North Star Bangle
ingredient: three thin slices of kamrakh (star fruit) in a little of their own juice
rhyme: the engraved north stars on the gold band = the star cross-section of kamrakh, gold on gold; star fruit is famously sour
notes: Shot from the gold listing photo (imported, 97b466d1) with the silver macro for the engraving only. 43a: slim flat polished gold band with the hinge, engraved eight-point stars each with a tiny stone alternating with round stones in flush bezels, as in the listing. Bangle about 1.3x a slice against about 0.8-1x true for a small kamrakh, within what the fruit allows. 43b equally faithful, bangle flatter and slices bleeding off the edge.

title: Droplet Open Ring
ingredient: a nimbu-mirchi: one kagzi lime and seven green chillies strung on a white cotton thread, the ring leaning on the lime
rhyme: the silver ball = the round lime, the silver teardrop = the tapering chilli; nimbu-mirchi is the charm hung at Indian doorways against the evil eye
notes: 44a/44b drew the ring about the width of the lime (true about half). Reshot leaning on a 4.5cm lime at the same depth with the chilli width as referent: 44d is 0.6 of the lime. Construction as the gold upright listing photo: thin band, a round ball at one end, and at the other a teardrop whose narrow neck runs into the band and whose round bulb is the free end, the two side by side across a small gap. 44c was true too but its chillies filled the top left.

title: Triple Coil Wrap Bangle
ingredient: bhakarwadi, a heap of spiral rounds with crumbs and sesame, one leaning on the bangle
rhyme: the coiled tubogas bangle = the rolled spiral of bhakarwadi, gold on golden-brown
notes: 46b: one continuous finely ribbed tubogas coil showing three lines at the front, two rectangular caps with two rows of pavé, one on the upper turn at the left and one on the lower turn, as in the listing. Bangle about 1.7x a bhakarwadi round, which suits a large 4cm piece. 46a was equally faithful with a cleaner prop layout but put a four-point star glint on the middle coil.

title: Garnet Cable Cuff
ingredient: dry rajma (red kidney beans), a loose heap with one bean against a garnet tip
rhyme: the deep garnet-red tips = glossy maroon rajma; rajma chawal is the North Indian Sunday lunch
notes: 47b: twisted silver rope cable, each end a gold barrel of three rings around two pavé rows, a faceted garnet in a gold bezel at each tip, the two garnets facing each other, as in the listing macro. Cuff about 4.8 beans across (true about 4.3); garnet about half a bean. 47a equally faithful, bean at the other tip and a busier top.

title: Charm Box Chain
ingredient: two motichoor laddoos, one whole and one broken open, with a few loose boondi
rhyme: the pavé barrel, packed with tiny points of light = motichoor, packed with tiny golden boondi (the name means crushed pearls); the broken laddoo is the idiom man mein laddoo phoota, a heart bursting with joy
notes: 48a/48b/48c each put a four-point star glint on the barrel; reshot forbidding star or cross sparkles. 48d: fine square box chain threaded through a barrel of three pavé bands between gold rims, as in the listing macro, no starburst. Barrel about five loose boondi long, true for 2mm motichoor boondi; the laddoos read small (about 3cm).

title: Serpentine Whisper Chain
ingredient: a wooden honey dipper letting one thread of honey fall into a small pool on the stone
rhyme: the fluid gold snake chain = a thread of honey, gold on gold; snake chains are prized for how they pour
notes: 49b: fine scaled gold snake chain, one cushion stone in four ball-tipped claws with an open basket gallery and a polished bail, as in the gold listing photos; chain clean and well apart from the honey. Stone about a third of the honey pool. The dipper is held from out of frame. 49a drew the stone larger and ran the chain close to the pool.

title: Baguette Tennis Necklace
ingredient: a fresh sprig of kadi patta (curry leaves) with loose leaflets
rhyme: one line of crosswise emerald baguettes beside the two neat rows of glossy curry leaves on their stalk; kadi patta is the last thing into every tadka
notes: Fiftieth slot: Pearl Circlet is on hold, so the second colourway of the Baguette Tennis Necklace (Emerald, 20 in stock; Crystal was shot 02). Shot from the emerald listing photo (imported, a3486d0b). 50b: crosswise emerald baguettes in gold box settings with side windows and corner claws, closed box clasp; the sprig runs parallel to the line. Baguette width about a fifth of a leaflet, true. The clasp carries a tiny illegible stamp. 50a was equally faithful with the clasp open and a busier layout.

title: Baguette Tennis Necklace
ingredient: a fresh mogra gajra, white jasmine buds strung tight on cotton thread
rhyme: a string of white jasmine buds = a string of clear baguettes, one inside the other; the gajra is gone by evening, the necklace is not
notes: 52a: crosswise clear baguettes in gold box settings with corner claws and side windows, the box clasp with its fold-over tongue at the front, as in the crystal listing; the clasp carries a tiny illegible stamp. The necklace line is about half a bud long, true for 6 mm and 14 mm. The gajra looks fresh: plump buds with green calyxes, a few open flowers, no browning. 52b was as faithful but cropped tighter, with the buds drawn large.

title: Woven Gold Hoops
ingredient: a golden silk paranda, a three-strand plait ending in a tassel bound with zari
rhyme: a braid of gold strands = a braid of golden silk; the school-day paranda, without the tangles
notes: 54b: both hoops an open braid of many polished gold strands, with flat polished discs capping the braid ends at the top and the thin hinged latch wire, as in the listing photos. Each hoop is about twice the plait's width, true for 25 mm hoops and a 12 mm plait. Clean S-curve with the hoops apart and a calm top left. 54a was as faithful, with one hoop over the plait and the tassel running out of the Feed crop.

title: Verdant Eternity Band
ingredient: a fresh money plant cutting, three marbled heart-shaped leaves on a short vine
rhyme: green ovals strung along a winding wave = heart-shaped leaves along a winding vine; the money plant every home grows, and the ring that grows on you
notes: 56b: oval emerald-green stones in claws set either side of one continuous S-wave of clear pavé, open back with looped tips, silver tone, as in the listing; the ring stands between the leaves, one leaf just overlapping its side. The ring is about two thirds of a leaf, true for a 2 cm band and small 3 cm leaves. 56a was as faithful but a soft clay pot crept into the calm top-left corner.

title: Baguette Tennis Bracelet
ingredient: the ivory keys of an old teak harmonium
ground: warm honey teak and old ivory keys
rhyme: a row of white crosswise baguettes = a row of white keys; a tiny keyboard laid on the big one
notes: 57c: crosswise clear baguettes in gold box settings with corner claws and the box clasp with its safety latches, as in the listing, laid diagonally across the keys; the black keys fall in true groups of two and three. About five baguettes to a key, true for 4 mm stones on 22 mm keys. 57a had the bracelet larger and straighter but drew the black keys in an even row with no gaps; 57b and 57d coiled the bracelet instead of laying it along the keys. A warm dark frame: the words sit in cream on the teak.

title: Silk Mesh Cuff
ingredient: a little cloud of white cotton wool
rhyme: the open C of a silver cuff = a crescent moon resting on a cloud; Chanda mama door ke, brought close
notes: 63a: one rounded tube of fine woven mesh bent into an open C with a polished flat oval cap on each end, silver tone, as in the silver listing; the cuff stands upright on the cotton like a crescent moon. The cuff is a little narrower than the cloud, true for 7 cm and an 8 cm puff. 63b laid the cuff flat across the cotton and cut it at the frame edge. A night-blue frame: the words sit in pale moon silver.

title: Brushed Gold Huggies
ingredient: an old wooden sewing spool wound with soft-gold zari thread
rhyme: the fine parallel brush lines of a satin finish = the fine parallel turns of gold thread on a spool; the same soft gold, spun two ways
notes: 65a: two chunky huggies of a wide softly domed band with a brushed satin finish of fine parallel lines and a hidden hinge, as in the listing; one leans on the spool and one sits in front. Each huggie is about half the spool's height, true for 14 mm and a 3 cm spool. The pale satin gold sits with the soft zari, so it reads gold, not silver. 65b was as faithful, with the thread running off the left edge.

title: Torsade Huggies
ingredient: a child's skipping rope of twisted cotton with a turned wooden handle
rhyme: polished gold ridges twisting round each huggie = the three-ply twist of a cotton skipping rope; the playground, in gold
notes: 69a: chunky domed huggies with polished twisted ridges all the way round and the hinge at the top, matching the listing and the earlier passed plate; one stands and one lies inside the coil of rope. Each huggie is about two and a half rope-widths tall, true for 20 mm and an 8 mm rope. Clean and crumb-free, unlike the retired khari shot (27). 69b was as faithful with the rope running off the right edge.

title: Molten Panel Bracelet
ingredient: a swatch of ivory net embroidered with rows of gold sequins (sitara), the edge of a lehenga dupatta
rhyme: rows of small flat oval gold plates = rows of gold sitara on a dupatta border; the festive shimmer, minus the scratch
notes: 70a: a flat articulated band of small flat oval gold plates in five staggered brick-set rows with a flat box clasp, as in the listing; no plate took on the sequins' round shape or holes. The bracelet is closed in a loop at the edge of the net. Each plate is a little longer than a sequin, true for 6 mm plates and 5 mm sitara. 70b was faithful with the band open flat and running off the right edge.
